title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1) Extended (v4)
shortDescription: Bank 1 downstream O2 sensor activity tracks the upstream too closely, indicating reduced catalyst storage.
fullDescription: Bank 1 downstream O2 sensor activity tracks the upstream too closely, indicating reduced catalyst storage. The PCM applies a moving-window average; persistent low oxygen storage triggers this code after multiple drive cycles. Cat efficiency can degrade from age, fuel contamination, oil consumption or sustained misfire.
safetyImpact: Most jurisdictions fail emissions inspection with this active; replacement may be required for registration.

causes.cause: Exhaust leak ahead of post-cat sensor

fixSteps.title: Read fuel trims
fixSteps.instruction: Verify long-term fuel trims are within +/-10%. Skewed trims point to upstream fuel issues that pre-fail catalysts.

fixSteps.title: Compare O2 waveforms
fixSteps.instruction: Capture upstream and downstream O2 traces at 2500 RPM. Downstream should be slow and flat; if it mirrors upstream, the cat is depleted.

fixSteps.title: Check for exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect manifold, flex pipe and bungs for cracks. False air entering before the rear sensor mimics this code.

fixSteps.title: Replace converter
fixSteps.instruction: If verified failed, replace with an OEM-grade or CARB/EPA-compliant converter. Aftermarket low-grade cats often re-fail within months.

faq.q: Will an O2 sensor fix this?
faq.a: Sometimes - if the sensor is slow, replacing it can clear the code. But genuine cat failure will not be masked by a sensor swap.

faq.q: Can I use a cat cleaner?
faq.a: Cleaners can buy a few thousand miles on a borderline cat. Severely depleted converters need replacement.

title: EVAP System Fault 0441 (v4)
shortDescription: EVAP system shows P0441 fault; sealed fuel-vapor system not holding or commanding correct purge.
fullDescription: EVAP system shows P0441 fault; sealed fuel-vapor system not holding or commanding correct purge. The PCM uses a vacuum decay or pressure-build test depending on platform; failure to reach or hold the commanded value sets a small/large/medium leak code or purge solenoid code as appropriate.
safetyImpact: EVAP faults are emissions-only and do not affect drivability beyond a possible faint fuel smell.

causes.cause: Purge solenoid stuck open or closed

fixSteps.title: Verify fuel cap
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect cap seal and tighten until clicks. A bad cap is the single most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Smoke-test EVAP system
fixSteps.instruction: With the vent commanded closed, introduce smoke at the service port. Trace any visible smoke to the leak source.

fixSteps.title: Bidirectional solenoid test
fixSteps.instruction: Command purge and vent solenoids on/off via scan tool while listening / observing flow. A non-responsive solenoid needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Inspect canister and lines
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the charcoal canister for cracks and saturation. Replace if fuel-soaked.

faq.q: Is this safe to ignore?
faq.a: It will not damage the engine, but will fail emissions and continue raw HC release.

faq.q: Why does it come back after I clear it?
faq.a: EVAP monitors run only under specific drive-cycle conditions; root-cause leaks return on the next valid monitor.

safetyImpact: EVAP faults are emissions-only and do not affect drivability beyond a possible faint fuel smell.

causes.cause: Purge solenoid stuck open or closed

fixSteps.title: Verify fuel cap
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect cap seal and tighten until clicks. A bad cap is the single most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Smoke-test EVAP system
fixSteps.instruction: With the vent commanded closed, introduce smoke at the service port. Trace any visible smoke to the leak source.

fixSteps.title: Bidirectional solenoid test
fixSteps.instruction: Command purge and vent solenoids on/off via scan tool while listening / observing flow. A non-responsive solenoid needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Inspect canister and lines
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the charcoal canister for cracks and saturation. Replace if fuel-soaked.

faq.q: Is this safe to ignore?
faq.a: It will not damage the engine, but will fail emissions and continue raw HC release.

faq.q: Why does it come back after I clear it?
faq.a: EVAP monitors run only under specific drive-cycle conditions; root-cause leaks return on the next valid monitor.

title: OBD-II Monitor Testing Not Complete (P1000) (EXT)
shortDescription: P1000 indicates OBD-II readiness monitors have not yet completed since the last code clear or battery disconnect.
fullDescription: P1000 indicates OBD-II readiness monitors have not yet completed since the last code clear or battery disconnect. This is not a fault per se; the vehicle simply needs a complete OEM drive cycle for catalyst, EVAP, EGR and O2 monitors to set ready. Inspection / smog will fail until clear.
safetyImpact: No drivability or safety impact; emissions test will fail until monitors complete.

causes.cause: Recent battery disconnect or DTC clear

fixSteps.title: Pull readiness monitors
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to view monitor status. Each monitor shows complete or incomplete.

fixSteps.title: Run OEM drive cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer drive cycle: cold start, idle, steady cruise, deceleration phases, multiple times.

fixSteps.title: Resolve pending DTCs
fixSteps.instruction: If a monitor refuses to set, check for pending codes - any pending fault can block its monitor.

fixSteps.title: Verify fuel level 30-70%
fixSteps.instruction: Some monitors (EVAP) require a specific fuel-level window to run. Top up or burn down accordingly.

faq.q: Why won't the monitors set?
faq.a: Most often the drive cycle was interrupted or a pending code is blocking. Resolve pending codes and repeat the drive cycle.

faq.q: Can I just clear it?
faq.a: P1000 is informational - clearing it just resets the readiness clock and does not help inspection.
